• SI unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω).

⇒ R = frac{{rho l}}{A}

Where R = resistance, l = length, A = area of cross-section and ρ = resistivity

EXPLANATION:__

 
• The wire is doubled on it means to fold the length of wire. That is its length will get half and the area of the cross-section will get doubled.

Given: R₁ = R = 4 Ω 

As we know that the resistance of the wire is,

Rightarrow R = frac{{rho l}}{A}

When the wire is doubled then, then its area will increase automatically. But the volume of the wire will be the same.

∴ The volume of original wire = volume of new wire

⇒ A1l1 = A2l2

⇒ A1l1 = A2 l₁/2

⇒ A2 = 2A1

 
• The resistance of the wire in 1st case

Rightarrow {R₁} = R = frac{{rho {l₁}}}{{{A₁}}} ----(1)

Rightarrow {R₂} = frac{{rho {l₂}}}{{{A₂}}} = ({rho {frac{l₁)/(2)}}}{{{2A₁}}} = frac{{rho {l₁}}}{{{4A₁}}} -----(2)

Divide equation 1 and 2, we get

⇒ R2 = 1 Ω

questions.question: Motion of a body with constant speed in a circular path is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uniform circular motion.**__

__
 
• The motion of a body with constant speed in a circular path is called **Uniform circular motion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Circular motion
 
 
• When an object moves along a circular path, then its motion is called circular motion e.g., the motion of a top.
 
• If an object moves along a **circular path with uniform speed**, its motion is called **uniform circular motion.**
 
• It is accelerated even if the speed of the body is constant. The motion of a satellite is an accelerated motion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Oscillatory Motion:
 
 
• If a particle **repeats its motion after a regular time interval** about a fixed point, motion is said to be oscillatory or vibratory.
 
• The motion of a piston in an automobile engine and the motion of the balance wheel of a watch are examples of oscillatory motion.
 
 
 
• In a non-uniform circular motion, an object’s motion is along a circle, but the **speed is not constant.**

questions.question: The inner and outer circumference of a circular ring is 22 cm and 44 cm respectively. What is the thickness of the ring ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.5 cm**__.

__
 
• The thickness of the ring is 3.5 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Circumference of circle is **2 × pi × r**

The inner circumference of a circular ring is **22 cm**.

So, 2 × pi × r = 22 cm.

⇒ r = {22 over 2 pi} = 3.5 cm.

The outer circumference of a circular ring is **44 cm**.

So, 2 × pi × r = 44 cm.

⇒ r = {44 over 2pi} = 7 cm.

So, The thickness of the ring = 7 - 3.5 = 3.5 cm.

questions.question: If Raj drives faster by 10 km/h, he reaches his village 90 minutes early. If he drives slower by 10 km/h, he reaches the village 150 minutes late. Find the distance he travels.
questions.solution:
**Given**:

If Raj drives faster by 10 km/h, he reaches his village 90 minutes early.

If he drives slower by 10 km/h, he reaches the village 150 minutes late.

**Concept Used**:

In this type of question, where distance remains constant, then speed varies inversely with time or vice-versa.

**Formula Used**:

Speed = distance/time

**Calculation:**

Let speed of Raj be ‘y’ km/h and time taken to reach his village by travelling at this speed be ‘z’ hours

When Raj drives faster by 10 km/h,

⇒ Speed of Raj = (y + 10) km/h

⇒ Time taken by him = (z – 3/2) hours

When he drives slower by 10 km/h,

Speed = (y – 10) km/h

Time taken by him = (z + 5/2) hours

⇒ (y + 10)(z – 3/2) = (y – 10)(z + 5/2) = (y)(z)

On equating we get

(y + 10)(z - 3/2) = yz

⇒ yz - 3y/2 + 10z - 15 = yz

⇒ 10z = 3y/2 + 15 ----(i)

(y - 10)(z + 5/2) = yz

⇒ yz + 5y/2 - 10z - 25 = yz

⇒ 10z = 5y/2 - 25 ----(ii)

(i) = (ii)

3y/2 + 15 = 5y/2 - 25

⇒ 5y/2 - 3y/2 = 15 + 25

⇒ y = 40

From (i),

10z = (5 × 40)/2 - 25 = 75

⇒ z = 75/10 = 7.5

⇒ y = 40 km/h and z = 7.5 hours

∴ Distance he travels = 40 × 7.5 = 300 km

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** If Raj drives faster by 10 km/h, he reaches his village 90 minutes early.

If he drives slower by 10 km/h, he reaches the village 150 minutes late.

⇒ {s(s+10)}over10 × 90over60 = {s(s-10)}over10 × 150over60

⇒ 3(s + 10) = 5(s - 10)

⇒ 3s + 30 = 5s - 50

⇒ 2s = 80

⇒ s = 40

The distance he travels = {s(s+10)}over10 × 90over60

⇒ {40×50}over10 × 90over60 = 300 km

**∴ The distance he travels is 300 km**

questions.question: The supplement of an angle is 15° more than three times its complement. The measure of the angle is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The supplement of any angle is always 90° more than its complement (C).

So, C + 90° = 3C + 15°

⇒ 2C = 75° ⇒ C = 37.5°

The required angle is 90° − C = 90° − 37.5° = 52.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 52.5°.**

The supplement of an angle is 15° more than three times its complement.

**Formula Used:**

Complement of an angle x = 90° − x

Supplement of an angle x = 180° − x

 
 
• 
 
 
• 
 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 

 

 
 
 x°
 90° − x°
 180° − x°
 
 
 O

**Calculation:**

⇒ 180° − x = 3 × (90° − x) + 15°

⇒ 180° − x = 270° − 3x + 15°

⇒ 180° − x = 285° − 3x

⇒ 3x − x = 285° − 180°

⇒ 2x = 105°

⇒ x = 52.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 52.5°.**

Two angles are complementary if their sum is exactly 90°. If one angle is θ, its complement is 90° − θ.

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are supplementary if their sum is exactly 180°. If one angle is θ, its supplement is 180° − θ.

For any given angle, the difference between its supplement and its complement is always constant and equals exactly 90°.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill an empty cistern in 15 hours while pipe B takes 25 hours to fill it. Initially pipe A is left open for some time and then closed and Pipe B is switched on immediately. In all the cistern takes 21 hours to be full. How long was Pipe A open?
questions.solution:
**Given**:

Two pipes A and B can fill an empty cistern in 15 hours and 25 hours respectively.

**Concept Used**:

In this type of question, individual efficiency of pipes is calculated.

**Formula Used**:

If a pipe ‘A’ can fill an empty cistern in ‘x’ hours then its efficiency is ‘1/x’.

**Calculation**:

Pipe A can fill an empty cistern in 15 hours

⇒ Quantity of cistern filled by pipe A in 1 hour = 1/15 units

Pipe B can fill an empty cistern in 25 hours

⇒ Quantity of cistern filled by pipe B in 1 hour = 1/25 units

Let initially pipe A was open for ‘y’ hours, then pipe B was opened for (21 – y) hours.

⇒ y/15 + (21 – y) /25 = 1

⇒ (5y + 63 – 3y) /75 = 1

⇒ (2y + 63) = 75

⇒ 2y = 12

⇒ y = 6 hours

∴ Pipe A was open for 6 hours.
